problem_statement: Write a program that takes a year as input and determines if it is a leap year. A leap year is divisible by 4, unless it is also divisible by 100 but not by 400. Given Input: year = 2024. Expected Output: 2024 is a leap year.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates whether the algorithm's logic accurately applies the leap year rules to produce the correct output for all valid year inputs.
sub_criteria: The algorithm correctly identifies years divisible by 4 as a primary condition for being a leap year.
The algorithm correctly applies the exception that years divisible by 100 are not leap years.
The algorithm correctly applies the sub-exception that years divisible by 400 are leap years despite being divisible by 100.
The algorithm combines these conditions using logically sound operators to arrive at the final leap year determination.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses if all necessary components of the algorithm are present, including input, output, and the core conditional checks.
sub_criteria: The algorithm describes taking a year as input.
The algorithm includes all necessary divisibility checks (by 4, by 100, and by 400).
The algorithm describes communicating the final determination (whether the year is a leap year or not).

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates how easy it is to understand the pseudocode's logic, focusing on clear language, logical flow, and unambiguous references.
sub_criteria: Each step of the algorithm is described using clear and understandable language.
The sequence of operations and logical decisions is easy to follow.
All variables or values referenced throughout the pseudocode are unambiguous in their meaning and purpose.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses the student's conceptual understanding of avoiding unnecessary computations or redundant steps in determining the leap year status.
sub_criteria: The algorithm avoids re-calculating divisibility conditions multiple times.
The algorithm determines the leap year status using a minimal set of logical comparisons.
